relationships.subject: substance P
relationships.evidence_quote: Application of SP (1 μM) on spinal cord slices resulted in an average 2.5‐fold increase in the number of spontaneous EPSPs arriving to lamina VII neurons

relationships.subject: SR140333
relationships.evidence_quote: The selective NK1 receptor antagonist, SR140333, did not block the EPSP increase at low concentration (10 nM) but abolished the effect of SP when applied at higher (50–200 nM) concentrations.

relationships.subject: tetrodotoxin
relationships.evidence_quote: In the presence of TTX (500 nM), blocking action potential generation, SP could not evoke EPSP number increase

relationships.subject: lamina I projection neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: neurokinin-1 receptors that, although being expressed in various lamina I neurons, are specifically enriched in PNs

key_findings: Full 3D reconstructions in rat show lamina I interneurons and projection neurons share nearly identical dendritic fields, but interneuron axons stay mostly in laminae I-III with lateromedial spread, whereas projection neuron collaterals target the dorsolateral funiculus and laminae IV-VI.

Substance P increased spontaneous EPSPs in lamina VII neurons via NK1 receptors in the superficial dorsal horn (blocked by SR140333, TTX, or dorsal horn removal), supporting a dorsoventral excitatory drive.
